results.title: Disciplinary procedures | HR Support
results.content: # Disciplinary procedures. ## Information about the University's procedures for dealing with disciplinary matters. It is the policy of the University to ensure that fair and effective arrangements exist for dealing with disciplinary issues, and to ensure that uniform standards are developed throughout the University with regard to both work and behaviour. Wherever practicable the formal procedures should be preceded by private and informal counselling. Day to day responsibility for disciplinary and related matters lies with the person to whom the member of staff reports and the relevant head of department. For academic staff, it rests with the head of department or faculty board chairman. These office holders are responsible, among other things, for clarifying the required standards, preliminary investigation of any concerns and for any private and informal counselling of those judged not to be meeting the required standard. Formal procedures for dealing with disciplinary and related matters are:. Please consult your HR Business Partner before initiating these procedures. From time to time departments may be named as respondent to an application made to an Employment Tribunal by an employee, ex-employee, or applicant for employment. When this occurs, the department will receive from the Regional Office of Employment Tribunals **form ET3**. Whenever a department receives this form, the appropriate HR Business Partner should be consulted immediately. Failing to meet the deadline may debar the University from taking any further part in the proceedings of the Tribunal - ie the University might effectively lose the right to defend the case in court. Within the 28 day period the applicant's claim has to be thoroughly investigated, the relevant statutory provisions checked, the facts of the case established, and the approach to defending the case decided. Valuable time will be lost if those who receive the ET form in the first instance do not act quickly. Departments therefore should ensure that those members of staff in the department who might be the first to receive form ET3 know of the need to refer the matter quickly to the Head of Department, or equivalent. The form should then be conveyed directly to the appropriate HR Business Partner in University HR by hand and without delay. * Statute XII, Part D: Discipline and Dismissal. * Statute XII, Part H: Appeals.

results.title: Disciplinary procedures
results.content:
Title: Disciplinary procedures
Disciplinary procedures are formal processes that employers use to address employee misconduct or performance issues. Employers must implement clear, consistent disciplinary policies to ensure that all employees are treated fairly. This guide outlines the key elements of a fair disciplinary process, best practices for employers, and common challenges in managing disciplinary cases. The transition from informal to formal disciplinary action should be clearly documented to ensure fairness and transparency. A structured disciplinary procedure ensures that actions taken against employees are fair and legally compliant. * **Notification**: Employees should be informed in writing about allegations, evidence, and potential consequences, including details of the disciplinary hearing. * **Disciplinary hearing**: Employees have the right to present their case, provide evidence, and be accompanied by a trade union representative or colleague. * **Appeal**: Employees have the right to appeal any disciplinary action, with the appeal reviewed by someone not involved in the original decision. ## Ensuring fairness in disciplinary procedures. Fairness in disciplinary procedures is essential for maintaining employee trust and avoiding legal challenges. Employees are more likely to accept disciplinary decisions when they feel they have been treated fairly. Employers who fail to follow fair disciplinary procedures may face serious consequences, including:. A well-defined disciplinary policy ensures that both employees and employers understand their rights and responsibilities. * **Detail the disciplinary process**: Include steps such as investigations, hearings, and appeal rights. To maintain fairness, disciplinary investigations must be thorough and impartial. Even in cases of serious misconduct, an employer must ensure that due process is followed to avoid legal claims. ### Conducting a fair disciplinary hearing. A disciplinary hearing provides an opportunity for both the employer and employee to present their case. Employees can appeal disciplinary decisions if they believe the process was unfair or the decision was unreasonable. Maintaining accurate disciplinary records is crucial for transparency, fairness, and legal compliance in UK employment law. Proper documentation supports fair decision-making, protects against legal disputes, and ensures compliance with the Acas Code of Practice. * **Acas code compliance** – Following the Acas Code ensures fair procedures and reduces legal risks. Accurate disciplinary records promote fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

results.title: Disciplinary Procedures for HR Professionals and Managers
results.content: Unstructured disciplinary action can lead to bias, legal risks, and low engagement among employees who feel the company is unpredictable and acting against them. Handling disciplinary action correctly requires a clear, consistent procedure that applies fairly to all employees. * **Progressive Disciplinary Procedures:** Progressive discipline involves a series of escalating steps designed to correct an employee's behavior. A well-defined disciplinary procedure ensures that all employees are treated fairly and consistently. When employees break company rules or don't follow proper procedures, disciplinary action may be needed. In some situations, especially where employees have legal protections against terminations, a hearing may be required before taking further disciplinary action. By following these steps, organizations can handle disciplinary issues in a structured and fair manner, ensuring that all employees are treated consistently and with respect. Effectively managing a disciplinary procedure requires clear documentation, consistent policies, and the right tools. * **Connected to Policy:** Clearly show how the employee’s actions violated company rules by connecting specific infractions to sections within your disciplinary policy or code of conduct.

results.title: Disciplinary and Grievance Procedures: Your questions answered. | IMD Corporate
results.content: This article will explore what disciplinary and grievance procedures are, the differences between them, why they are essential for employers, the risks of not having them, and the importance of handling these issues properly from the outset. Disciplinary procedures are employer-led, initiated by the employer to address issues with an employee’s conduct or performance. On the other hand, grievance procedures are initiated by the employee to address concerns about their employment conditions or treatment. ## Why should UK employers have disciplinary and grievance procedures and policies? The Acas Code of Practice on Disciplinary and Grievance Procedures (the Acas Code) sets out the standard that employers are expected to meet. Failing to have clear disciplinary and grievance procedures in place, or not following them correctly, exposes employers to several risks:. Addressing issues promptly and effectively can prevent them from escalating into more serious problems or disputes, while following the correct procedures offers strong legal protection if a case is taken to an Employment Tribunal.

results.title: Disciplinary Procedures Training Programme | Methods, resources
results.content: Comprehensive training programmes play a vital role in preparing employees and managers to navigate disciplinary procedures effectively. These programmes are instrumental in equipping individuals with the necessary knowledge and skills to ensure fairness, consistency and adherence to legal and organisational guidelines throughout the disciplinary process. Training programmes can be an important foundation in achieving these objectives by providing participants with a thorough understanding of the legal frameworks and organisational policies that govern disciplinary proceedings. By focusing on the legal framework component in training programmes, organisations can equip their employees and managers with the necessary knowledge and understanding to navigate disciplinary procedures effectively and ethically within the UK legal context. Organisational policies and procedures regarding disciplinary actions are essential for ensuring consistency, fairness and compliance within the workplace. This includes managers, who are responsible for identifying and addressing performance or conduct issues promptly and fairly, initiating disciplinary procedures as necessary and ensuring compliance with company policies and legal requirements. By clearly defining these policies, procedures, roles and responsibilities, organisations can ensure consistency in handling disciplinary matters, promote a fair and respectful workplace environment and minimise the risk of legal disputes. Training programmes should include practical exercises, case studies and role-playing scenarios to reinforce these principles and enhance participants’ skills in managing disciplinary processes effectively. By integrating conflict resolution and mediation skills into training programmes, organisations empower their managers and HR professionals to handle disciplinary situations with sensitivity, professionalism and effectiveness. Integrating these principles into training programmes ensures that managers and HR professionals are well-equipped to uphold high standards of fairness and equity in all aspects of disciplinary decision-making. By diversifying delivery methods and providing access to a variety of educational resources, organisations can accommodate different learning preferences and maximise the effectiveness of training programmes on disciplinary procedures. Training programmes focused on disciplinary procedures offer numerous benefits to both employees and the organisation as a whole, including improving employee confidence. Training programmes focused on disciplinary procedures play an important role in ensuring fairness, consistency and compliance within organisations. By equipping employees and managers with the necessary knowledge and skills, these programmes promote a deeper understanding of legal frameworks and organisational policies governing disciplinary actions.
